simple.meaning: אָיֹם (ʼâyôm) is a Hebrew word meaning “frightful.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אָיֹם (H366) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Song of Songs 6:4, with occurrences in Song of Solomon, Habakkuk.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָיֹם (H366) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אָיֹם (H366) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אָיֹם (ʼâyôm) / H366 is traced through Song of Songs 6:4, Song of Songs 6:10, Habakkuk 1:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H366. ayom אָיֹם adjective terrible, dreadful — terrible , of Chaldeans הוּא וְנוֺרָא אָיֹם Hab 1:7 ; of dignified woman, awe-inspiring כַּנִּדְגָלוֺת אֲיֻמָּה Song 6:4 , 10 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root (meaning to frighten);

occurrences.englishText: They are feared and dreaded. Their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves.
